confirmed.roadmap_row: ROADMAP §4.2 M: "Trash with restore (soft delete, auto-purge after N days)" (M1)
confirmed.summary: Auto-purge after the retention period is not implemented in any client. Soft delete, restore and manual purge work in rv and the web vault. The predicate `ItemMerge::purge_due` (30-day retention measured from the trash HLC) exists in rizzy-sync and has unit tests, but no client ever calls it, so trashed items are never purged automatically. Per ADR 0012 §5 only clients purge, and the server worker must not purge trash (ADR 0022), so nothing purges the trash today.

The only tests are crates/rizzy-sync/src/merge/tests.rs:351-364. `grep -rn -E "purge_due|may_purge|TRASH_RETENTION|autoPurge|auto_purge" crates apps packages`, outside rizzy-sync/src/merge* and rizzy-core/src/item, returns nothing: no caller in rizzy-client, rizzy-wasm, rizzy-cli, packages/core or apps/web. The only purge paths are manual: rizzy-client/src/items.rs:485 `purge_item`, rv `item purge` (crates/rizzy-cli/src/args.rs:671), web ItemView 'purgeItem' (apps/web/src/views/ItemView.tsx:373). ADR 0022 worker row: "**Does not purge trash** (ADR 0010 §1)". ADR 0018 §12 also asks for the unit test "no auto-purge while an unknown-version restore is parked" at the client level. Only the sync-level predicate test with holds_unapplied=true exists (merge/tests.rs:364).
confirmed.governing_adrs: ADR 0012: "Status: Partially superseded by [ADR 0018] (...§5 in part...); [ADR 0021] (...); [ADR 0022] (... §5 in part ..., owner decisions 3, 5 and 8 ...); [ADR 0032] (§7 in part)". The §5 Purge bullet ("manually, or automatically once an item has been in the trash for the retention period. The default is 30 days... any device may issue it") is not superseded. ADR 0022 only rewords the Server-mode sentence and keeps the 30-day default. ADR 0018: "Status: Accepted" (§9 Trashed at / retention; §11 "No purge over an unapplied record"). verdict.reason: I could not refute it. A grep for purge_due, may_purge, TRASH_RETENTION, auto_purge, autoPurge, purgeDue and retention across crates, apps and packages finds no caller outside crates/rizzy-sync/src/merge* and crates/rizzy-core/src/item. Every purge path in rizzy-client, rizzy-wasm, rv and the web app is manual: VaultSync::purge_item at crates/rizzy-client/src/items.rs:485, Session::purge_item / purgeItem at crates/rizzy-wasm/src/session.rs:466, the device.rs purgeItem, and rv `item purge`. The predicates exist and are unit-tested: ItemMerge::purge_due and may_purge (crates/rizzy-sync/src/merge.rs ~1130-1145), DEFAULT_TRASH_RETENTION_MS and purge_due_ms in crates/rizzy-core/src/item/display.rs. The client already has the unapplied-record check: VaultSync::holds_unapplied at crates/rizzy-client/src/sync.rs:1368. The server must not purge (ADR 0022 worker row: "Does not purge trash"), so no component ever runs the auto-purge. No doc moves it to a later milestone. ROADMAP §4.2 lists it as Must for M1, and ADR 0018 cites that row. There is no docs/HANDOFF.md. ADR 0018 §12 also asks for a unit test, "no auto-purge while an unknown-version restore is parked", and it has no client-level version: the only test is the rizzy-sync predicate test.
verdict.corrected_adr_gate:
accepted_adr_covers. This is client behaviour that issues an existing op type (Purge); it adds no new format or crypto. The ADRs that cover it:
- ADR 0012 §5 "Purge" bullet: "manually, or automatically once an item has been in the trash for the retention period... 30 days, measured against the trash op's HLC... any device may issue it". ADR 0012 is Partially superseded. ADR 0022 (Accepted) only rewords the third sentence of "Only clients purge" to "Auto-purge happens only when some client is online after the retention period." and restates decision 3 with trash retention 30 days. ADR 0018 (Accepted) adds to §5 and does not remove the auto-purge.
- ADR 0018 (Status: Accepted) §9 "Trashed at" (the retention runs from it), §11 "No purge over an unapplied record ... manual or automatic", and §12 for the required unit test.
- ADR 0022 (Accepted): the server worker does not purge trash.

confirmed.roadmap_row: ROADMAP §4.2 M: "Password history per item" (M1)
confirmed.summary: Password history is stored but no client can show it. The merge keeps up to 50 history entries per field, and per ADR 0012 §5 and ADR 0018 §7 the history of `login.password` is the password history. No public client API returns it, and neither rv nor the web vault shows it. Only the export path reads it, through an internal helper (`state::password_history`). Imported `pwhist/<id>/…` entries appear in the web vault only as raw unrecognised keys in the 'other' group.
confirmed.evidence: crates/rizzy-sync/src/merge.rs public ItemMerge API (lines 611-1168) has field/lifecycle/times/purge_due but no history accessor. crates/rizzy-client/src/items.rs public read API (item_lifecycle, item_type, field_value, field_conflicts, field_keys at :530-567) has no history accessor. The only reader is crates/rizzy-client/src/export/payload.rs:425 `state::password_history(live)`, used for export. `grep -rn -i "history|pwhist"` over apps/web/src, packages/core/src, crates/rizzy-cli/src and crates/rizzy-wasm/src finds only the generator's own value history, import 'historyNotCarried' counts and docs/rv.md:90 ('Tags and password history have no order'). It finds no view. apps/web/src/fields.ts:151-160 groups only uri/field/passkey lists, and every other list (pwhist) goes to `other`. Web e2e (apps/web/e2e/*.spec.ts) and rv e2e have no password-history check.
confirmed.governing_adrs: ADR 0012: "Status: Partially superseded by [ADR 0018] (... §5 in part ...); [ADR 0021] (...); [ADR 0022] (...); [ADR 0032] (§7 in part)". §5 "Password history (M1) is the history of `login.password`" is still binding. I could not refute the gap, so it is real. One part of the evidence is wrong, but that does not change the conclusion.

What I checked:
- ROADMAP row: docs/ROADMAP.md:77 "Password history per item" is Must, M1, with no deferral. ADR 0012 §5 says "Password history (M1) is the history of `login.password`". ADR 0018 §7 (line 199) says the same, and ADR 0018:202 adds `pwhist/<id>/value · /ms` for history imported from another manager. docs/HANDOFF.md does not exist, and no other doc moves the history view to a later milestone.
- Correction: the sync layer does expose the history. `ItemMerge::field()` in crates/rizzy-sync/src/merge.rs:1078 is public and returns `FieldView { current, history, display }`, and `FieldView.history` at :477 is a pub field. So "no history accessor in ItemMerge" is false. The gap starts one layer up, in rizzy-client.
- rizzy-client: the public read API in crates/rizzy-client/src/items.rs:530-567 is `item_lifecycle`, `item_type`, `field_value`, `field_conflicts` and `field_keys`. None returns history. The only reader is `pub(crate) fn password_history` in crates/rizzy-client/src/export/state.rs:107, used by export/payload.rs. client lists.rs supports `pwhist` elements in general, but only as list elements for display and edit validation, not as a history view.
- rizzy-wasm: nothing returns history. Its only history items are the import `historyNotCarried` count and the `own_history_ahead` sync flag.
- rv: `item_show` in crates/rizzy-cli/src/commands.rs:377-420 loops over `field_keys` and `field_value`, so it never shows the merge history of `login.password`. Imported `pwhist/<id>/value` and `/ms` keys print only as raw key/value lines.
- Web vault: apps/web/src has no history view. The only history there is GeneratorPane's own list of generated values. apps/web/test/fields.test.ts:73 confirms that `pwhist` keys land in the `other` group.

verdict.corrected_adr_gate:

Its History bullet (line 98, "every value removed from a register goes into the item's history") and its §7 `login.password` row ("The history of `login.password` is the password history (ADR 0012 §5)") bind the meaning, and `pwhist/…` is defined at line 202. ADR 0013 §3 rule 3 (reveal only on the user's request; the web vault Worker sends only summaries and revealed values to the UI thread) governs how to expose the values.

This work is a read-only view over existing state. It adds no new crypto, wire format or persistent format, so no new ADR is needed. If the API sends history values across the wasm/Worker boundary, they must follow the ADR 0013 reveal rule.

confirmed.roadmap_row: ROADMAP §4.2 M: "Trash with restore (soft delete, auto-purge after N days)" (M1), the purge and trash semantics of ADR 0012 §5 and ADR 0018 §3
confirmed.summary: The client-side surfacing rules for trash and purge are not wired anywhere. The first is the notice for an edit that arrives after a permanent delete ("An edit from Laptop arrived for an item you deleted permanently. Restore it as a new item?"), with restore-as-new-item from the late registers. The second is the "deleted on X while it was being edited on Y" notice when Active wins over a concurrent trash. The sync engine keeps the data, through `late_values_to_surface` and `mark_surfaced`, but no client calls these functions, so late edits stay invisible in the tombstone. Note: the general "edited on Phone and Laptop at the same time" conflict UI is a separate ROADMAP §4.5 M3 row. These purge and trash notices are not named there, but the owner may consider them part of that row.
confirmed.evidence: crates/rizzy-sync/src/merge.rs:1151 `pub fn late_values_to_surface`, :1168 `pub fn mark_surfaced`. `grep -rn -E "late_values_to_surface|mark_surfaced|lateValues|deleted on|while it was being edited"` over crates/rizzy-client/src, crates/rizzy-wasm/src, crates/rizzy-cli/src, packages/core/src and apps/web/src gives no hits.
confirmed.governing_adrs: ADR 0018: "Status: Accepted" (§3 "Surfacing": "A device shows this notice once for late values it has not yet surfaced ... Restoring creates a new item"). ADR 0012: "Status: Partially superseded by [ADR 0018] (... §5 in part ...); [ADR 0021] (...); [ADR 0022] (...); [ADR 0032] (§7 in part)". The §5 Trash bullet ("The edited item stays visible, with a notice: 'deleted on X while it was being edited on Y'") is not superseded. ROADMAP §4.5 "Clear conflict UI" row: M3.

verdict.reason: I could not refute it. The sync engine provides the API: crates/rizzy-sync/src/merge.rs:1151 `late_values_to_surface` and :1168 `mark_surfaced`. They are tested in merge/tests.rs:496 and :571 and exercised in proptests.rs:473 and fuzz/fuzz_targets/sync_merge.rs:373. No consumer exists anywhere outside rizzy-sync, its tests, its fuzz target and the spike. I grepped every .rs/.ts/.tsx/.md file in the repo, which covers crates/rizzy-client, rizzy-wasm, rizzy-cli, packages/core, apps/web and apps/extension. rizzy-client/src/items.rs implements trash, restore and purge and exposes `item_lifecycle` (Absent/Active/Trashed/Purged). Nothing in it reports late values in a tombstone, restore-as-new from them, or a concurrent trash that lost to Active. The web UI (apps/web/src/views/ItemView.tsx) only has the Trash, Restore and Purge buttons. No doc moves this work elsewhere: docs/HANDOFF.md does not exist, and ROADMAP has no row for these notices. The §4.5 M3 "Clear conflict UI" row is about field edit conflicts ("edited on Phone and Laptop"). The surfacing rules are part of the M1 trash and purge semantics that ADR 0012 §5 and ADR 0018 §3 specify. One caveat: the owner may choose to read the M3 conflict UI row as covering the "deleted on X while edited on Y" notice. The core purge notice ("Restore it as a new item?") is tied to the M1 Trash row.
verdict.corrected_adr_gate: accepted_adr_covers. ADR 0018 is Status: Accepted. Its §3 "Surfacing" says this is "local presentation and changes no bytes", and restoring creates a new item from the displayed late register values (§6). Line 35 of ADR 0018 restates "Active wins over a concurrent trash". The ADR 0012 §5 Trash and "Late ops after a purge" bullets are still binding: ADR 0018 supersedes §5 only in part, for the tombstone layout and history, and does not touch the notice text. Neither notice involves any wire or format change. Gate limit: the `surfaced` dot set is in-memory evidence of ItemMerge. merge.rs:131 says "rizzy-client persists them", but the ADR 0026 cache (Accepted) has no slot for surfaced dots. Persisting "shown once" across restarts by adding a new field or record to the local cache is therefore a persistent-format change and needs an ADR 0026 amendment (a new Proposed ADR) first. Without that, the surfaced set can only live in session memory, or be derived from data the cache already holds.
verdict.implementation_notes:
Files to change:
- crates/rizzy-client/src/items.rs, in VaultSync:
  - Add `late_edits_to_surface()`. It returns, for each tombstoned item with unsurfaced late values, the item id, the dots and the originating device ids. The device name comes from the device directory or account state.
  - Add `mark_late_edits_surfaced(item)`, which calls `ItemMerge::mark_surfaced`.
  - Add `restore_late_as_new_item(item, item_type, rng)`. It reads the displayed values of the tombstone's late registers and creates a new item through the existing `create_item` path (`WriteMode::Create`). The user confirms the type (ADR 0018 §3, §6).
  - For "deleted on X while edited on Y": expose a query that reports when an item's `@lifecycle` register holds concurrent Trashed and Active values while Active displays. It returns the trash dot's device and the edit's device. This may need a small accessor on ItemMerge in crates/rizzy-sync/src/merge.rs that returns the `@lifecycle` current values with their dots. The read-only accessor must keep the redacted Debug.
- crates/rizzy-wasm/src/items.rs and session.rs: bindings for these calls.
- packages/core/src/index.ts, apps/web/src/protocol.ts and core-worker.ts: RPC plumbing.
- apps/web/src/views/VaultView.tsx and ItemView.tsx: render a one-time banner or dialog with the ADR-exact texts "An edit from <device> arrived for an item you deleted permanently. Restore it as a new item?" and "deleted on <X> while it was being edited on <Y>". Add the restore-as-new flow with a type picker.
- Optionally rizzy-cli: `rv` commands to list late edits and restore one.

Persistence: keep the surfaced set in memory only, which means the notice shows once per unlock session. Persisting it needs an ADR 0026 change first, so flag that to the owner rather than extending the cache format. No secrets in Debug or errors: late values are decrypted content and stay in zeroizing types.

Tests:
- rizzy-client tests: a purge concurrent with an offline edit gives exactly one surfaced entry. `mark` clears it. Restore-as-new creates a new item id with the late values, and the tombstone stays purged. A concurrent trash and edit shows Active plus the notice data.

confirmed.summary: The INV-15 canary test does not exist. INV-15 (M1) says the master password, Secret Key, recovery code, account key, vault keys, item keys and private keys never leave a client unencrypted, and its verification is a canary test: create an account with known secrets, run every flow, then search every HTTP body, DB row, log line and backup file for them (raw, hex, base64). (raw, hex, base64)'). docs/CRYPTO.md §15 item 5, last bullet ('Canary: the E_dev, E_local, E_ks and ACCOUNT_KEY_FORWARD envelope bytes never appear in any request body or server row'). `rg -i canary crates` returns 0 hits, and `rg 'INV-15' crates apps packages fuzz` returns 0 hits (INV-15 is the only M1 invariant of the key-secrecy kind cited nowhere in code). verdict.reason:
I could not refute the gap. The INV-15 canary is required at M1 in four places: THREAT_MODEL.md:1114 (INV-15), INV-2 (:1090) and INV-48 (:1177), which both cite "Canary test (INV-15)" as their verification, and ADR 0011 "No plaintext" (docs/adr/0011-storage.md:130), which says "The INV-15 canary test exercises every flow, dumps both databases, and searches them for the known secrets." That part of 0011 is not among the parts ADR 0022 supersedes, so it is still binding. CRYPTO.md:1389 (§15 item 5) also asks for an E_dev/E_local/E_ks/ACCOUNT_KEY_FORWARD canary. No code implements any of this. `rg -i canary` finds only docs and a wordlist entry, and `rg INV-15` finds nothing in crates. The secret-search tests that do exist cover something else:
- crates/rizzy-server/tests/drill.rs:435-571 searches DB rows and backups for the server secrets file only.
- crates/rizzy-domain-auth/tests/auth/secrets.rs:~140-200 checks that the server DB holds no server-side secrets (INV-8/INV-50: session token, TOTP secret, OPAQUE setup, enum key, data key, recovery token). It never looks for the client's master password, Secret Key, recovery code, account key, vault keys, item keys or private keys.
- crates/rizzy-cli/tests/e2e.rs:783-788 and crates/rizzy-cli/tests/account.rs:646-655 search only the local client sqlite cache for the password, SK and recovery-code text.
None of these looks at HTTP bodies, server DB rows or log lines for the client secrets, and none checks hex or base64 encodings. docs/HANDOFF.md does not exist, and no doc moves this work to a later milestone. The ROADMAP row it falls under is line 104, "Secret memory hygiene" (M1).
verdict.corrected_adr_gate: no_adr_needed. The work is a test that checks an existing invariant. It adds no crypto, auth, wire or persistent format, and it does not change any security boundary. The requirement is already authorized by the binding part of ADR 0011 "No plaintext" (Status: Partially superseded by ADR 0022, but the "No plaintext" section is not among the superseded parts), together with THREAT_MODEL INV-15/INV-48 and CRYPTO.md §15 item 5. Stop if the test cannot reach key bytes without a new public API or an export of key material: making production code reveal keys would touch a security boundary and needs the owner's input. Use a #[cfg(test)] or dev-only path instead, or capture the bytes from the client-side test harness.
verdict.implementation_notes:
Where to put it: a new integration test, e.g. crates/rizzy-cli/tests/canary.rs, or a module in crates/rizzy-server/tests/http/ if driving rizzy-client directly is simpler. Reuse the harness in crates/rizzy-cli/tests/e2e.rs, which starts the server and drives `rv` and already has an HTTP proxy that reads raw requests (around e2e.rs:323). Extend that proxy to record every request and response body.

Steps:
1) Choose known secrets: a fixed master password, then the SK and recovery code printed at signup. Caveat: the `notify` role is M3 (ADR 0010). Any pull-based M1 signal, such as a field in the account view, would be a wire change that no Accepted ADR defines. So whether this is an M1 gap or an accepted M3 deferral is the owner's call.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute the gap. The ADR 0008 decision 5 text cited here is not named by ADR 0022 point 7, so it is still binding. It says a valid code opens a pending recovery and that "every enrolled device and the account email (if mail is configured) are notified". CRYPTO.md §11.9 step 2 (lines 1124-1128) and step 6 (line 1141) say the same, and so do THREAT_MODEL Q-15 and §351 ("the enrolled devices are notified"). The ROADMAP M1 row (line 108) covers the recovery story. No document moves device notification to a later milestone. The only deferral is a code comment in crates/rizzy-domain-auth/src/recovery.rs:24-26 ("has no M1 channel (the notify role and mail are M3)").

There is no notification today. `RecoveryPending` (recovery.rs:55) is returned to the server but nothing consumes it. rizzy-proto defines no pending-recovery field outside recovery.rs, and AccountView has none. The only recovery message that touches a pending recovery is `recovery/cancel`, which reports whether one was pending. ADR 0028 item 50 confirms this. Because cancel has a side effect, a device cannot use it to check status. docs/HANDOFF.md does not exist.

Two things partly soften the gap:
- Email notification is legitimately M3, because SMTP relay is M3 under ADR 0010 and 0022.
- The push channel, the `notify` role, is M3 under ADR 0010.

Device notification by itself has no scheduled home, though, and without it the 72 h cancel window does not protect a user whose kit was stolen. The ADR gate does block implementation: any pull-based signal (a field in AccountView, or a `recovery/status` endpoint) is a change to the wire format and the security boundary, and no Accepted ADR defines one. ADR 0028 lists only `recovery/start`, `recovery/complete` and `recovery/cancel`. The gap is real, but closing it needs an owner decision first: either a new Proposed ADR, or an owner-approved ROADMAP/ADR note that defers device notification to M3 together with the notify role.
verdict.corrected_adr_gate: needs_new_or_proposed_adr. ADR 0008 decision 5 is binding and requires that devices are notified, but it defines no mechanism. ADR 0010 puts the `notify` push role in M3. ADR 0028, which is Accepted with some parts superseded by 0031 and 0032, lists only the start, complete and cancel recovery endpoints and no status signal. Any M1 pull-based signal is a wire and security-boundary change, so it needs a new ADR (Proposed, then Accepted by the owner) or an ADR 0028 amendment before any code is written. The alternative is that the owner explicitly records the deferral to M3 in ROADMAP. Do not write code until the owner decides.

confirmed.roadmap_row: M | Auth that never sends a password-equivalent: OPAQUE (loss of server_setup, CRYPTO.md §5.8)
confirmed.summary: If an operator loses the OPAQUE server_setup and has no restorable copy, there is no supported way back. CRYPTO.md §5.8 says that after a loss 'the admin marks the records invalid' and clients then re-register from an enrolled device or use recovery. The server CLI has only `secrets init`, `secrets rotate` and `secrets retire-setups`, and every one of them needs the existing setup or a DB that matches it. The startup check refuses a new secrets file against the old DB (SetupMismatch). The self-hosting guide documents this lockout, but its stated reason is wrong: it says the API has no re-registration, recovery, password-change, device-revocation or key-rotation request, and all of these exist.

When the admin marks the records invalid, the client re-registers OPAQUE'). crates/rizzy-server/src/cli.rs:217-250 (parse_secrets: only init, rotate, retire-setups). crates/rizzy-domain-auth/src/secrets.rs:453-456 (SetupMismatch on a hash mismatch). `rg -i 'invalidat|records invalid' crates/rizzy-server/src crates/rizzy-domain-auth/src` returns no hits. Contradicted doc: docs/self-hosting.md:211 ('Gap: this build has no re-registration or recovery endpoint ... no OPAQUE re-registration, recovery, password-change, device-revocation or key-rotation request'), against crates/rizzy-proto/src/http.rs:98 ACCOUNT_REREGISTER_START, :100 ACCOUNT_COMMIT, :120-124 RECOVERY_START/CANCEL/COMPLETE.
confirmed.governing_adrs: ADR 0003: 'Status: Partially superseded by [ADR 0022](0022-server-mode-only.md) (point 10)' (cites §5.8 for rotation only); ADR 0031: 'Status: Accepted' (covers retiring setups that are still held, not loss); ADR 0010: 'Status: Partially superseded by [ADR 0022](0022-server-mode-only.md) (§1 in part)'. No Accepted ADR names an operator command for the loss case. The self-hosting.md:211 correction is docs-only.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute the gap and could not. CRYPTO.md §5.8 says that after losing server_setup "the admin marks the records invalid" and clients then re-register or recover. No operator path does that:
- crates/rizzy-server/src/cli.rs parse_secrets accepts only init, rotate and retire-setups.
- In crates/rizzy-domain-auth/src/secrets.rs, check_database refuses to start in two cases. If the new secrets file reuses an existing setup_id with a different key hash, it returns SetupMismatch. If the database holds credential records and no loaded setup is recorded there, it returns NoRecordedSetup.
- It also returns MissingDataKey when sealed TOTP or login-state rows name a data_key_id that is not loaded. So losing the whole secrets file also blocks startup through the data keys, not only through OPAQUE.
- retire-setups only retires setups that are still loaded and have a recorded successor (ADR 0031). It cannot retire a setup whose secrets are gone, and it needs a startable configuration.

No ROADMAP, HANDOFF or ADR row schedules a loss-recovery command anywhere else. ADR 0042, the only ADR above 0041, is Proposed and about account-settings layout, so it is unrelated.

The doc contradiction also holds. docs/self-hosting.md:211 says the API has no re-registration, recovery, password-change, device-revocation or key-rotation request. crates/rizzy-proto/src/http.rs:98-160 defines ACCOUNT_REREGISTER_START, ACCOUNT_COMMIT and RECOVERY_START/CANCEL/COMPLETE.

The lockout conclusion on that line stays true in practice: the server will not start, so those endpoints cannot be reached. Only the stated reason is wrong.

confirmed.summary: `rv recovery complete` (like `rv login`) saves no pending state before the server answers, because ADR 0026 defines no pending stage for it. If the answer is lost, the user cannot tell which Emergency Kit is valid and may be left with an extra enrolled device. rv.md records this as 'an open point'. The interrupted-commit handling already exists for signup, rotation and credential changes, but not for recovery.

verdict.reason: The gap could not be refuted. crates/rizzy-cli/src/recover.rs (module docs, lines 23-39, and the outcome_unknown branch around lines 174-180) says outright that `rv recovery complete` persists nothing before the commit and cannot use the byte-identical repeat from ADR 0028. docs/rv.md:126 calls this "an open point". ADR 0026 (Accepted) defines only `stage: 1 committed | 2 signup-pending` in the device_state record (line 44). Its stage-2 rule needs a RegisterFinishRequest, and its pending record/pending_commit (lines 56, 84) assume an already-committed device state. So it has no recovery-pending stage and no CommitChangeRequest-from-no-state form. CRYPTO.md §11 "Secrets before commit" step 3 still expects a durable client to persist a pending record before upload, and recovery is one of the cases it names. That is a doc/ADR mismatch, not a scheduled item. I found no Proposed ADR that addresses it: the only Proposed ADRs are 0033 and 0042, neither related, and no "stage = 3" or recovery-pending format exists anywhere in docs or crates. The ROADMAP M1 row "Recovery story written down and implemented" covers it. The implementation is already labelled as a reported open gap waiting on the owner, so the gap is real but ADR-blocked. Fixing it means defining a new persistent format, a new device_state stage, so it cannot be done under the existing Accepted ADRs.
verdict.corrected_adr_gate: needs_new_or_proposed_adr. A new ADR (Status: Proposed) partially superseding ADR 0026 §2/§3 has to add a recovery-pending device_state stage, e.g. stage 3, holding the new SK/device_salt/kdf_id/E_local plus pending_commit with the byte-identical CommitChangeRequest for the recovery commit. It also needs restart/resend semantics under ADR 0028's byte-identical-repeat rule and parsing invariants. Optionally it should cover a login/enrol pending stage too. The owner must accept it before any code. No code is authorized now: ADR 0026 is Accepted but defines no such stage, and ADR 0008 (Partially superseded by 0022 point 7) covers recovery semantics, not this persistent format.
verdict.implementation_notes: Blocked until the owner accepts a new ADR. Update docs/rv.md:126 and the recover.rs module docs. confirmed.roadmap_row: §4.6 M: Single sync engine (op log, HLC, VV, field merge, tombstones) / Server mode compaction into snapshots
confirmed.summary: Known convergence bug that is still open. A paged Fetch can put a tombstone cover in one page and its recorded purge (a later link of the same chain) in the next. The merge then refuses the tombstone (PurgeAboveCut), the chain stops at a gap and the cursor does not move. Every later Fetch with the same paging repeats this, so the device never converges, even against an honest server. The real server does page: at most PAGE_MAX_OPS ops per page, MAX_RECORDS = 4096. The test pins the stall instead of a fix, and no rule settles it.
confirmed.evidence: crates/rizzy-sync/src/convergence/named.rs:503-514: test `finding_a_paged_tombstone_cover_split_from_its_purge_stalls`, documented as 'Finding (reported, not fixed here) ... against an honest server the device never converges ... ADR 0021 §4 ... and the spike ... leave this open'. crates/rizzy-sync/src/convergence.rs 'Findings' section says the same. The production server pages: crates/rizzy-domain-vault/src/fetch.rs:11-35, 63-67 (PAGE_MAX_OPS, PAGE_BYTES, `complete: false`). grep for PurgeAboveCut or a workaround in crates/rizzy-client/src: none. The merge refusal is at crates/rizzy-sync/src/merge.rs:310.
confirmed.governing_adrs: ADR 0021 'Status: Partially superseded by [ADR 0032](0032-healing-rotation-after-backup.md) (§9 "Healing request" in part)'. §4 'Each page of a paged response carries its own covers' does not settle the case. ADR 0018 'Status: Accepted' (§3 'Snapshots are claims'). ADR 0012 'Status: Partially superseded by [ADR 0018] (§1 in part, §3 in part, §4 in part, §5 in part, §6 in part, §7 in part, §12 in part); [ADR 0021] (§6 in part, §7 in part); [ADR 0022] (Milestone line, §5 in part, §6 in part, §8, §9 in part, §10, §11, §12 in part, owner decisions 3, 5 and 8, Risks in part); [ADR 0032] (§7 in part)'.

verdict.reason: I could not refute it, and the evidence for it is strong. The code itself says the bug is open. crates/rizzy-sync/src/convergence/named.rs:500-547 has a test, finding_a_paged_tombstone_cover_split_from_its_purge_stalls, marked "Finding (reported, not fixed here)". It checks that the stall happens: paged_refused > 0, the chain head stays at 0, and verdict().is_err(). The "Findings" section of crates/rizzy-sync/src/convergence.rs:53-57 says the same, and so do world.rs:567-571 and device.rs:101 and 1001. The production server can produce the split. crates/rizzy-domain-vault/src/fetch.rs pages at PAGE_MAX_OPS = MAX_RECORDS/2 ops and a PAGE_BYTES budget, and its module docs say "a page stops inside one device's chain only". It only guarantees that a bodiless header and its covers land on the same page. It does not keep a tombstone cover on the same page as the purge op that comes later in the same chain, and it cannot, because the purge dot is inside the encrypted snapshot. The grep found no handling of PurgeAboveCut and no paging workaround in crates/rizzy-client/src. No document schedules a fix elsewhere: docs/HANDOFF.md does not exist, the ROADMAP has no row for it, and the only ADR text on paging is ADR 0021 §4 line 81 ("Each page of a paged response carries its own covers"), which does not cover this case. This is a convergence (liveness) failure on the M1 "Single sync engine" ROADMAP row (line 167).
verdict.implementation_notes:
Blocked until the owner accepts an ADR. The likely fix is on the client side, in rizzy-sync's merge driver and in rizzy-client's fetch loop: keep a cover refused as PurgeAboveCut on a page that is a strict prefix (complete == false), and merge it again after later pages raise the verified cut. Do not advance the cursor past the gap until that happens. The alternative is a server rule that extends a page to the end of the chain. The server cannot see the purge dot, so that rule would have to be "never stop a page inside a chain that has bodiless headers of an item with a tombstone cover", or similar.

The mechanisms being modelled are rotation (CRYPTO.md §11.6 under ADR 0025) and ITEM_KEY_WRAP / vault-key epochs (ADR 0018 and others). Each has an Accepted ADR, and the harness must use the existing rizzy-core primitives without inventing anything. verdict.implementation_notes:
Files:
- crates/rizzy-sync/src/convergence/{world.rs, device.rs, server.rs, generate.rs, faults.rs, checker.rs, crypto.rs, named.rs}
- the module doc table in crates/rizzy-sync/src/convergence.rs, rows 22-24 and the "Crypto" paragraph at 45-51

Constraint on crate direction: rizzy-sync may depend only on rizzy-core, and its dev-dependencies are only proptest, chacha20 and rand_core. The rotation logic in rizzy-client therefore cannot be reused. The harness has to model rotation with rizzy-core primitives:
- vault key epochs
- sealing ITEM_KEY_WRAP envelopes
- vault_key_epoch in headers (rizzy-core envelope/purpose.rs, sign/statements.rs)
- the writer rule: a fresh item key on the first write after a rotation

Approach:
1. Add a `rotation` history family. A device's revocation triggers a vault-key epoch bump: new item-key wraps go only to non-revoked devices, and a server stale-epoch check rejects old-epoch ops and snapshots per ADR 0021 §9.
2. Device reaction to a stale-epoch answer: process the new account-state, then re-issue with the same device_seq only the ops the server itself rejected as stale. An op that may have been stored and served is re-published in a healing request instead (the "already stored" path).
3. Kind-4 (durable) authors: their snapshots are accepted only up to last_accepted_device_seq, and refused after expiry.
4. Raise the faulty-device bound to two or more, beyond the f + 1 two-author covers. The checker must then accept "detected and reported" in place of convergence where ADR 0021 §9 "Restored-server revocation" or the bound says so.

New checker properties:
- **ADR 0012 §12 property 6:** for every revoked device, check that no envelope written after the rotation epoch opens under any key that device holds. Try decrypting with its held item keys and wraps, and assert that every attempt fails.
- INV-19-style: old-epoch keys open no post-rotation object.
- ADR 0021 §9 "Stale epoch": no stale op is stored except the listed exceptions, and the re-issued op keeps its device_seq.
- Convergence, no silent loss and gap detection still hold with rotation interleaved with purges, snapshots and restores.

- Add named regression scenarios: a stale answer lost across a restore, and a kind-4 snapshot after expiry.
- Update the module doc table so the "not reached" row is removed or narrowed.
- Keep the PR budget at 1,000 cases per property, plus the nightly run.

confirmed.roadmap_row: §4.9 M: Structured logging with no secrets (and INV-15 'never leaves the client unencrypted')
confirmed.summary: The INV-15 canary test, which INV-48 extends to logs at the most verbose level, does not exist. Nothing creates an account with known secrets, exercises every flow, and then searches every HTTP body, database row, log line (at debug) and backup file for those secrets in raw, hex and base64 form. 'No secrets in logs' holds by construction (allow-listed fields in log.rs) but has no end-to-end test. The e2e tests send the server's stderr to /dev/null.
confirmed.evidence: `grep -rni 'canary\|INV-15' crates apps packages`: no test. docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:1114 (INV-15: '**Canary test**: create an account with known secrets, exercise every flow, then search every HTTP body, DB row, log line and backup file'). docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:1177 (INV-48: 'Canary test (INV-15) extended to logs at the most verbose level'). docs/adr/0011-storage.md:129 ('The INV-15 canary test exercises every flow, dumps both databases...'). crates/rizzy-cli/tests/e2e.rs:171-173 and crates/rizzy-cli/tests/account.rs:123-125 spawn the server with .stderr(Stdio::null()). The only log tests are unit tests in crates/rizzy-server/src/log.rs:157-181. drill.rs checks only that server secrets are absent from the backup (INV-50).
confirmed.governing_adrs: ADR 0011 (status line as in G5; the 'No plaintext' section binds). ADR 0010 'Status: Partially superseded by [ADR 0022](0022-server-mode-only.md) (§1 in part)'. THREAT_MODEL INV-15 and INV-48 are normative requirements (docs/README.md).

verdict.reason: The gap is real, but the claim overstates it a little. Partial secret-absence checks already exist. crates/rizzy-cli/tests/e2e.rs:783-788 checks that the master password, Secret Key and recovery code are absent from the client cache file, raw form only. crates/rizzy-cli/tests/account.rs:645-653 repeats that check after a Secret Key change. crates/rizzy-domain-auth/tests/auth/secrets.rs:170-203 dumps the server DB and checks that server-side secrets (tokens, enum/data keys, OPAQUE setup) are absent. drill.rs covers server secrets in backups (INV-50). No test does what INV-15/INV-48 (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:1114, 1177) and ADR 0011 'No plaintext' (docs/adr/0011-storage.md:129) require: create an account with known client secrets, run every flow, then search HTTP bodies, server DB rows, server log lines at RIZZY_LOG_LEVEL=debug and backup files, in raw, hex and base64 form. No test file names 'canary' or INV-15. The e2e harnesses (e2e.rs:173, account.rs:125, healing.rs:148) still send server stderr to Stdio::null(), so nothing reads the logs. Logging has a debug level (crates/rizzy-server/src/log.rs:39-61, RIZZY_LOG_LEVEL), so the test can be built. The ROADMAP §4.9 row 'Structured logging with no secrets' is M1, and the invariants are M1. HANDOFF.md does not exist, and no doc schedules this work for later.
verdict.corrected_adr_gate: accepted_adr_covers. This work only adds a test and changes no crypto, protocol, wire or persistent format. ADR 0011's 'No plaintext' section is not among the parts ADR 0022 supersedes (status line: point 9 in part, Transactions/concurrency in part, 'What is stored, by sync mode', Backups in part), so it binds, and it requires the INV-15 canary test. THREAT_MODEL INV-15/INV-48 are normative and name it as their verification. No new ADR is needed. The test must not change log fields or formats; if it finds a leak, fixing that leak is a separate change.
verdict.implementation_notes:
Add a canary integration test, for example crates/rizzy-cli/tests/canary.rs, or extend the e2e.rs harness. Steps:
1. Start the rizzy-vault server with RIZZY_LOG_LEVEL=debug. Pipe stderr to a file or buffer instead of Stdio::null(); a shared helper option would also cover e2e.rs, account.rs and healing.rs.
2. Capture HTTP bodies. Either put a recording TCP proxy between rv and the server (e2e.rs already parses raw HTTP at about line 323), or drive the flows through rizzy-server's HTTP test harness (crates/rizzy-server/tests/http/common.rs).
3. Run signup with fixed, known secrets (master password, captured Secret Key, recovery code). Then run login, item create/edit/sync on two devices, password change, Secret Key change/rotation, recovery, export/import, and device add/revoke.
4. Run `rizzy-vault backup --out` and read the file. Dump the server DB through the storage dump API (as in secrets.rs).
5. Search every captured byte stream (HTTP request and response bodies, DB rows, log lines, backup file, client cache) for each secret in raw, lowercase/uppercase hex and base64 standard/url, padded and unpadded.
6. Add the account key, vault keys and item keys, which the client exposes only in test builds, if a test hook is available. If no hook exists, cover the user-facing secrets and say plainly that the key-level checks are not done; do not add an unsafe or production-visible accessor.
Keep all unwrap calls in test code. Check that the base64/hex crates are already dev-dependencies, so the test adds no new crate. Mention INV-15/INV-48 in the doc comment. If the test takes long, consider gating it like the existing e2e tests, but it must run in CI. A Postgres variant is optional, following the pattern in crates/rizzy-storage/tests/storage/postgres.rs.

confirmed.roadmap_row: §4.9 M: Backup & restore command + documented procedure (tested, not just written)
confirmed.summary: The secrets half of backup and restore is incomplete. `rizzy-vault backup-secrets` writes an encrypted file, but no command reads it back, so a backup-secrets file alone cannot be restored. The operator guide says to keep a separate age/gpg copy instead. The lost-secrets path in CRYPTO.md §5.8 ('When the admin marks the records invalid, the client re-registers OPAQUE') has no admin command either. The server refuses to start when the secrets do not match the database, and no Accepted ADR names a command for either case.
confirmed.evidence: docs/self-hosting.md:171: '> **Gap: no command reads the encrypted backup yet.** No Accepted ADR names a command that restores the secrets from a `backup-secrets` file, so this build has none'. docs/self-hosting.md:459: '...once the command that reads it exists'. The command parser crates/rizzy-server/src/cli.rs:221-324 has init, rotate, retire-setups, serve, migrate, backup-secrets, backup and restore, but no secrets restore and no records-invalidation command. docs/CRYPTO.md:391. `grep -rni 'restore-secrets\|marks the records' docs/adr`: no match.
confirmed.governing_adrs: ADR 0011 (status line as in G5; 'Backups' in part superseded by 0022, and owner decision 3 encrypts the backup but names no reader). ADR 0010 'Status: Partially superseded by [ADR 0022](0022-server-mode-only.md) (§1 in part)'. ADR 0023 'Status: Accepted' covers only the database backup file. No Accepted ADR covers a secrets-restore or records-invalidation command.

verdict.reason: I could not refute the gap. `crates/rizzy-server/src/secrets_backup.rs:129` has `pub fn open()`, which decrypts a backup-secrets file. Only unit tests at lines 185-197 call it, so no command uses it. The `secrets` subcommand parser in `crates/rizzy-server/src/cli.rs` (lines 221-237) has only init, rotate and retire-setups, with no restore and no records-invalidation command. `docs/self-hosting.md:171` states the gap itself and gives age/gpg copies of secrets.json as the only restore path; line 459 says the same. ADR 0011 'Backups' (lines 137-138) and owner decision 3 (line 175) name only the writer (`backup-secrets`). ADR 0023 step 4 tells the operator to 'restore the secrets first' but defines no command for it. ADR 0028 item 13 fixes the JSON layout of the backup file and says a reader exists, which is the module function, not a CLI. CRYPTO.md §5.8 (around line 391) says 'When the admin marks the records invalid, the client re-registers', but no admin command or ADR implements that. A grep of docs/adr finds no secrets-restore or invalidation mechanism. No Proposed ADR covers either (ADR 0042 is unrelated). The ROADMAP §4.9 M1 row 'Backup & restore command ... tested' governs, and a backup file that cannot be restored leaves the secrets half incomplete. Possible counterpoint: the documented age copy is a manual workaround, so some may see this as a doc-level limitation rather than a missing M1 feature. But the project's own docs call it a gap and say it is gated on an ADR.
verdict.corrected_adr_gate: needs_new_or_proposed_adr. Writing secrets.json from a backup crosses a security boundary: it installs OPAQUE setups, the enum_key, data keys and the bootstrap token, and it interacts with retired-setup checks (ADR 0031 point 6) and with the startup check in CRYPTO §5.8. Marking OPAQUE records invalid changes the authentication and record state. ADR 0011 'Backups' is Accepted only in part (partially superseded by 0022). It and ADR 0023 (Accepted) name no reader command and no invalidation command, so no Accepted ADR authorizes either. The owner must accept a new ADR first. Agents may only draft it as Proposed and add its README row.
verdict.implementation_notes:
The owner must accept a new ADR before any code is written. Draft it as Proposed from docs/adr/0000-template.md and add a row in docs/adr/README.md. It needs to specify:
- `rizzy-vault secrets restore-backup <file>` (name to be decided), which reads the passphrase from stdin like backup-secrets, calls `secrets_backup::open`, and parses the result with the existing secrets_file parser (ADR 0028 item 13 layout, at most 256 KiB, unknown members refused).
- Whether it refuses to overwrite an existing secrets.json, writes mode 0600 atomically, requires the server stopped (writer lock or instance lock per ADR 0010 §2 and ADR 0023), refuses a setup the DB marks retired (ADR 0031 point 6), and checks the setups against the DB's AKE public-key hashes.
- For the lost-secrets case: an admin command, for example `secrets reset-opaque`, that generates a new setup, marks the records under lost setups invalid (or retired, reusing ADR 0031's fake-record path), and lets the server start. Clients with a device session then re-register as CRYPTO §5.8 describes. Decide whether this reuses `retired_at_ms` semantics or needs a new column, which would be a migration.

Files once accepted:
- crates/rizzy-server/src/cli.rs (new subcommands and usage text)
- crates/rizzy-server/src/admin.rs (handlers, lock acquisition)
- crates/rizzy-server/src/secrets_backup.rs and secrets_file.rs (writer path)
- the storage layer, if records are invalidated
- docs/self-hosting.md §5 and §10 (remove the Gap note and add the passphrase drill)
- docs/CRYPTO.md §5.8 and §5.11 (name the commands)

Tests:
- integration (SQLite, in-process): backup-secrets → wipe the secrets volume → restore-backup → serve passes the startup check; wrong passphrase refused; existing file not overwritten; a retired setup in the backup refused; the server running refused.
- lost-secrets: reset the OPAQUE setup, then a device-session client re-registers and a web-only user recovers.
- extend the CI restore drill to cover the secrets.
- fuzzing: the existing server-secrets parsers likely cover the new input, but confirm.

confirmed.roadmap_row: §4.9 M: Rate limiting, lockout/backoff on auth (DoS mitigations: per-account quotas)
confirmed.summary: No per-account storage quota is enforced. THREAT_MODEL A15 and §7.6 'D' list per-account quotas as the control against op floods and storage exhaustion. ADR 0021 owner decision 2 puts no per-item cap on retained snapshots because 'the account storage quota bounds the bytes', but no such quota exists. Only per-request body limits are enforced (RIZZY_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES). ADR 0028 item 3's closed error table has no quota error code, so adding one is a wire-protocol change.
confirmed.evidence: `grep -rni 'quota' crates/rizzy-server/src crates/rizzy-domain-vault/src`: no match. Only the per-request body limit exists: crates/rizzy-server/src/http/api.rs:488-490 and crates/rizzy-server/src/config.rs:91. docs/adr/0021-server-compaction.md:96, 146 and 186 rely on 'the account storage quota'. docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:257, 643 ('Per-account quotas and body-size limits') and 936. docs/adr/0028-api-v1-http-conventions.md:22 (closed error-code list).
confirmed.governing_adrs: ADR 0021 'Status: Partially superseded by [ADR 0032](0032-healing-rotation-after-backup.md) (§9 "Healing request" in part)' (owner decision 2 assumes a quota). ADR 0028 'Status: Partially superseded by [ADR 0031](0031-retiring-old-opaque-setups.md) (item 3 in part); [ADR 0032](0032-healing-rotation-after-backup.md) (item 3 in part)'. No Accepted ADR defines the quota (size, scope, error code).

verdict.reason: I couldn't refute it. A grep for 'quota' across every .rs file in the workspace finds only one hit, a doc comment at crates/rizzy-sync/src/compaction.rs:97 that assumes "the account storage quota bounds both". No crate enforces one: not rizzy-server, rizzy-domain-vault, rizzy-storage or rizzy-domain-auth. rizzy-domain-auth's rate-limit buckets only count auth attempts (login, TOTP, registration); they don't cap stored bytes or ops. The only size controls are per request: the 1 MiB default body limit, RIZZY_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES and the 8-slot large-body semaphore (ADR 0028 items 7-8). The docs depend on a quota that doesn't exist. THREAT_MODEL.md:643 lists "Per-account quotas and body-size limits" among the A15 mitigations, and §7.6 'D' (line 936) names quotas as the control against op floods and storage exhaustion. ADR 0021 (lines 96, 146, 186; owner decision 2) leaves retained snapshots uncapped per item on the grounds that the storage quota bounds the bytes. No ADR anywhere defines the quota, and no later milestone or ADR schedules it. One caveat weakens the scoping. ROADMAP §4.9 line 224 actually reads "Rate limiting, lockout/backoff on auth, security headers, CSP on web vault | M1" and doesn't name quotas. The claim's roadmap_row text, "DoS mitigations: per-account quotas", is a paraphrase. Treating quotas as M1 rests on the threat model and ADR 0021's assumption, not on explicit ROADMAP wording, so the owner should confirm that quotas belong to this row or M1. That doesn't change the finding that the control the docs rely on is missing.
verdict.corrected_adr_gate: needs_new_or_proposed_adr. No Accepted ADR, and no surviving part of a Partially superseded one, sets the quota's scope, size or default, how it is configured, how stored bytes are counted (persistent state), or what the server answers when it's exceeded. ADR 0028 item 3 fixes a closed error-code set: invalid_request, client_too_old, unauthorized, second_factor_required, fresh_session_required, not_found, state_conflict, stale_epoch, record_conflict, prev_seq_mismatch, api_version_gone, payload_too_large, rate_limited, internal. Reusing 413 payload_too_large or 429 rate_limited for "quota exceeded" would still change the meaning of a wire-protocol answer, and item 3 says the set stays closed, so a new code needs an ADR that supersedes item 3 in part. Item 12 also fixes the closed list of RIZZY_* settings, so a new quota setting would be another configuration change that needs an ADR. Every option needs a Proposed ADR the owner accepts. The scope question (whether quotas belong to the ROADMAP row) also goes to the owner.
verdict.implementation_notes:
Blocked until the owner accepts a new ADR that partially supersedes ADR 0028 items 3 and 12. Once it exists:
(1) Count stored bytes per account. Either keep a running counter in the vault tables, updated in the same transaction as each upload, heal or commit and as compaction deletes records, under ADR 0011's per-account lock; or sum sizes on demand. A counter column needs a rizzy-storage migration.
(2) Enforce the quota in rizzy-domain-vault (upload.rs and the heal and commit paths) before the insert. Compaction and deletion must lower the count. The quota must not stop key rotation, healing or revocation from completing: the same anti-lockout reasoning as THREAT_MODEL A15. A sensible design lets ops that free space through even when over quota.
(3) Add a config setting in crates/rizzy-server/src/config.rs, an ErrorCode variant in rizzy-proto error.rs, and its status mapping in crates/rizzy-server/src/http/api.rs (around lines 488-510; header test around line 1213).
(4) Tests: an over-quota upload is refused with the agreed code; a heal or rotation while over quota is allowed if the ADR says so; the count drops after compaction; property tests show the count matches the sum of stored bytes across upload, compaction and restore; the header or error-table test pins the new code.
(5) Docs: once the ADR is in, update THREAT_MODEL A15 and §7.6, the ADR 0021 cross-reference and the crates/rizzy-sync/src/compaction.rs:97 comment so they point to it.
Medium size.

confirmed.summary: No client reads the global list, and no client stores the highest list_version it has accepted. `global_list()` has no caller outside rizzy-match, and the wasm matcher always passes an empty equivalence view. So once a list ships it will still not reach matching, and the INV-39 no-downgrade check has no persisted state to compare against. ADR 0038 §2 says clients persist the highest list_version, but no ADR sets where or in what bytes (ADR 0026's device_state has no such field).
confirmed.evidence: `grep -rn 'global_list\|highest_accepted\|list_version'` outside crates/rizzy-match/src finds only crates/xtask (the signer) and a rizzy-core doc comment, with no caller in rizzy-client, rizzy-wasm or apps. crates/rizzy-wasm/src/matching.rs:13-21 module docs say 'Deferred ... every decision runs against EquivalenceView::empty'; :205 is `let equivalence = EquivalenceView::empty();`. `grep -n list_version docs/adr/0026-*.md` finds nothing.
confirmed.governing_adrs: ADR 0038 '- Status: Accepted' (§2 requires persisting the highest list_version); ADR 0037 '- Status: Accepted' (§7 merged view); ADR 0026 (cache/device-state format) has no field for it

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. The evidence holds up.

1. `rizzy_match::compiled::global_list(highest_accepted_version)` (crates/rizzy-match/src/compiled.rs:49) has no caller outside rizzy-match. The only other `list_version` hits are the xtask signer and a doc comment in rizzy-core sign/mod.rs:719.
2. crates/rizzy-wasm/src/matching.rs:13-21 says the equivalence settings are deferred. Line 206 hard-codes `EquivalenceView::empty()`. In crates/rizzy-client/src/matching.rs, every `EquivalenceView::empty()` I saw is in tests. There is no production path that builds a view from the global list.
3. Nothing stores a highest accepted list_version. ADR 0026 (Accepted) lists exactly which keys `cache_meta` holds and which values must never go backwards (state_seq, settings_seq, bundle_seq, identity_epoch and others). list_version is not among them. A grep of ADR 0026 and crates/rizzy-client/src/store for equivalen, list_version and INV-39 finds nothing.
4. ADR 0038 §2 (Accepted, line 49) requires clients to persist the highest accepted list_version "alongside the other monotonic state INV-25 already tracks". THREAT_MODEL INV-39 says the same, so the requirement is binding and unmet.

Two points reduce how urgent this is but do not refute it:
- No list ships yet. `compiled::GLOBAL_LIST = None` and `LIST_SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY = None`, so `global_list` returns `Ok(None)` today. The missing wiring has no effect until a list is signed and compiled in, which is itself an M2 deliverable.
- No other doc schedules this work elsewhere. ADR 0042 (Proposed, 2026-10-08) covers only the ACCOUNT_SETTINGS side: the disabled groups and user-defined groups. It does not cover the persisted list_version.

I also found a latent bug the gap description misses. `EquivalenceList::verify` (crates/rizzy-match/src/equivalence.rs:388) rejects `list_version <= highest_accepted_version`. A client that persists the version it accepted and then re-verifies the same compiled-in list on its next launch would reject its own list, and equivalence matching would silently fall back to plain registrable-domain matching. The persistence design has to accept an equal version with identical bytes (or the same signed hash) and reject only a lower version, or an equal version with different bytes. That is a reading of INV-39 the owner needs to confirm, because INV-39 literally says "equal or lower".
verdict.corrected_adr_gate:
The gap splits into two parts with different gates.

(a) Wiring `global_list()` into the merged EquivalenceView inside rizzy-client and rizzy-wasm (ADR 0037 §7, ADR 0038 §5) is authorized by those Accepted ADRs. The account's disabled and user-defined groups also feed that view, and reading them depends on ADR 0042, which is only Proposed. So only the global-list half of the view can be built now.

(b) Persisting the highest accepted list_version is new persistent state in the ADR 0026 device-state/cache file, either a new `cache_meta` key or a new column, plus a new never-goes-backwards rule. ADR 0026 is Accepted and does not provide for it. Per CLAUDE.md, a persistent-format change needs an Accepted ADR, so this part is needs_new_or_proposed_adr: a new Proposed ADR that partially supersedes ADR 0026 (ADR 0020 point 9). The owner must also confirm how "equal version" is treated (see reason).
verdict.implementation_notes:
Files involved:
- crates/rizzy-match/src/compiled.rs: `global_list`, with `GLOBAL_LIST` and `LIST_SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY` both `None` today.
- crates/rizzy-match/src/equivalence.rs:353-433: `verify`, which rejects `<=` at line 388.
- crates/rizzy-client/src/matching.rs: needs a production function that builds `EquivalenceView::new(global, &disabled, &user_groups)`.
- crates/rizzy-client/src/store/: needs the persisted floor, once an ADR allows it.
- crates/rizzy-wasm/src/matching.rs:206: replace `EquivalenceView::empty()` with the view built by the client. The committed expansion baseline crates/rizzy-wasm/generated/expanded.rs has to be regenerated with it.

Steps:
1. Draft a Proposed ADR, for example 0043, that partially supersedes ADR 0026. It should:
   - add a `cache_meta` key, e.g. `equiv_list_version` as u32 big-endian, or decide the value lives per device rather than per account;
   - add it to the "never goes backwards" list;
   - set the migration and format bump (cache_meta.format 1→2);
   - define acceptance as: an equal version is accepted when the bytes or signed hash match, and a lower version is rejected. This would change `verify`'s comparison or add a separate same-list check.
   Add the README row. Do not touch any Status line.
2. After the ADR is Accepted, implement the following:
   - In rizzy-client, on unlock or load, read the floor, call `global_list(floor)` and store the new floor in the same transaction. On error, fall back to user-only groups, never to an unverified list.

3. Tests:
   - A lower version is rejected.
   - The same list on a second launch is still accepted (regression for the `<=` bug).

   - A wasm matching test proves a group from a fixture list yields a MatchedVia equivalence candidate. Use a fixture list signed with a test key, since no real list or key exists yet.

critic_additions.roadmap_row: §4.3 M: KDF: Argon2id ... versioned params, client-side (ADR 0004)
critic_additions.summary: The INV-6 per-flow Argon2id count test does not exist. INV-6 (M1) gives a fixed number of Argon2id runs for each flow, as an 'instrumented test counting KSF calls per flow against that table'. The table: enrolled-device unlock and web login, 1; durable signup and first login on a new device, 2; web signup, 1; re-enrolment after rotation, 2; Server-mode password change, 3. The only counter is `opaque::ksf::test_hooks::ksf_runs`, which is pub(crate) and cfg(test) inside rizzy-core. It counts only the OPAQUE KSF, not the local-wrap `kdf::argon2id` runs, and only rizzy-core/src/opaque/tests.rs uses it. The flows themselves live in rizzy-client, which has no way to count runs, so no test checks any row of the INV-6 table.
critic_additions.evidence: `grep -rn 'ksf_runs|argon2id_runs|kdf_runs'` over crates/ matches only crates/rizzy-core/src/opaque/ksf.rs:166 (the definition) and crates/rizzy-core/src/opaque/tests.rs. crates/rizzy-core/src/kdf.rs `argon2id()` has no test counter, and its only cfg(test) hook is the wipe observer. No counting test exists in crates/rizzy-client/src/tests*.rs or crates/rizzy-cli/tests. Table: docs/THREAT_MODEL.md INV-6 row (line ~1094), and CRYPTO.md §5.4 and §11.

critic_additions.roadmap_row: §4.4 M: Security rules: never autofill HTTPS-saved credentials on HTTP; never autofill into cross-origin iframes by default; autofill on user gesture only
critic_additions.summary: The end-to-end tests with adversarial pages that INV-37 names as its verification are missing. The rules themselves are in place. rizzy-match/src/security.rs has `https_downgrade_blocks`, called from modes.rs, and it has unit tests. The content script runs in the top frame only (`all_frames: false`, `window.top === window`) and checks CSS visibility and the topmost element. But the extension's Playwright suite has no page that is HTTP holding an HTTPS-saved login, no cross-origin iframe page and no hidden-field page (display:none, visibility:hidden, opacity:0). The only adversarial e2e tests cover a visually covered field and an untrusted synthetic click (INV-36). This is separate from G9, which is about the suite not running in CI and about Firefox: the test cases themselves do not exist.
critic_additions.evidence: The test list of apps/extension/e2e/*.spec.ts, from `grep -nE '^\s*test\('`, covers enrol/autofill/save, service worker, offscreen, popup, storage.session, the covered-field topmost check, trusted and untrusted clicks, 6-minute idle, passkeys, and the save-prompt race. None of them covers an HTTP page, an iframe or a hidden field. The only INV-37 references are in crates/rizzy-match/src/security.rs and modes.rs. critic_additions.roadmap_row: §4.4 M: Browser extension: Chromium (MV3) + Firefox — inline menu, fill, save/update on submit
critic_additions.summary: The 'manifest check in CI' that INV-40 requires does not exist. Today it holds only by inspection: neither manifest declares `externally_connectable`, and content scripts use `all_frames: false`. No xtask check, unit test or CI step reads apps/extension/manifest.chromium.json or manifest.firefox.json. So adding `externally_connectable` for web origins, web-accessible resources for secret UI, or `all_frames: true` would not fail any check. `cargo xtask check-js` checks only package.json files (crates/xtask/src/js.rs `manifests()` collects package.json). ci.yml has no step for the extension.

Only apps/extension/vite.config.ts copies the files. crates/xtask/src/js.rs:167-199 checks package.json only. .github/workflows/ci.yml has no extension-specific step. critic_additions.roadmap_row: §4.4 M: Browser extension: Chromium (MV3) + Firefox (key custody)
critic_additions.summary: The INV-63 verification test is missing. INV-63 says unlocked key material is never written to storage.local, storage.sync or IndexedDB, and that only wrapped device state is persisted. Its verification is a 'test that inspects every extension storage area after unlock and after a worker restart'. No unit or e2e test inspects storage.local, storage.sync, IndexedDB or storage.session after unlock or after a worker restart. The existing storage tests check only that account config and the cache work: account-config.test.ts and idb.test.ts use a fake IndexedDB, and the e2e test checks that storage.session survives a popup reload. The rule is recorded only in comments in apps/extension/src/core-host/session-store.ts.
